card.name: Words right before a work's title
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as called, in, of, and 's just before the title of a book, opera, or newspaper in historical or literary prose. The next word is usually a capitalized title.

modes.label: Link before a title
modes.description: A word like called, in, or 's directly introduces the title of a literary or musical work.
modes.example: Another intriguing bit of writing came after Moby Dick in 1866, when Melville published a volume of poetry<< called>> Battle-Pieces and Aspects of the

modes.label: Possessive after an author
modes.description: An author's name followed by 's or in, leading into the title of their work.
modes.example: Other notable examples include Thomas Hardy<<'s>> Tess of the d'Urberv

modes.label: Of or in before a named work
modes.description: A small word after a noun like premiere or editorial, ahead of a named work or publication.
modes.example: ON DECEMBER I0, 1910, the Metropolitan Opera gave the world premier<< of>> an opera by the most famous living Italian
